Here's what changed and why:

**`BTreeNode` is now a `private static` nested class inside `BTree`** — this is the main structural fix. Previously `BTreeNode` was a package-visible class, meaning any code in the same package could construct nodes, call `insertNonFull`, `splitChild`, etc. directly, bypassing `BTree`'s invariants entirely. As a `private static` inner class it's truly hidden — it can't be named or referenced outside `BTree`. `BTreeNode.java` is deleted.

**`search()` → `containsKey()` returning `boolean`** — the old `search()` returned `BTreeNode` for the sole purpose of a `!= null` check in `BTree.contains()`. Returning the node was an internal implementation detail leaking through the method signature. The new `containsKey()` returns a `boolean` directly, which is all any caller needs, and the name no longer clashes with `BTree.contains()`.

**`minDegree` and `leaf` marked `final` in `BTreeNode`** — both are set in the constructor and never mutated. Making them `final` documents this invariant and lets the compiler enforce it.

Previously `BTreeNode` was a package-visible class, meaning any code in the same package could construct nodes, call `insertNonFull`, `splitChild`, etc. directly, bypassing `BTree`'s invariants entirely. As a `private static` inner class it's truly hidden — it can't be named or referenced outside `BTree`. `BTreeNode.java` is deleted.

**`search()` → `containsKey()` returning `boolean`** — the old `search()` returned `BTreeNode` for the sole purpose of a `!= null` check in `BTree.contains()`. Returning the node was an internal implementation detail leaking through the method signature. The new `containsKey()` returns a `boolean` directly, which is all any caller needs, and the name no longer clashes with `BTree.contains()`.

**`minDegree` and `leaf` marked `final` in `BTreeNode`** — both are set in the constructor and never mutated. Making them `final` documents this invariant and lets the compiler enforce it.
